extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark and automated multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation. It comprises 1,825 diverse tasks across nine domains to evaluate LLMs on generating dynamic, interactive visual artifacts based on source code and temporal execution screenshots guided by fine-grained checklists.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics such as state changes, animations, and responsiveness.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A two-stage filtering process was applied: MinHash and semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, followed by screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Prompts were rewritten by experts and LLMs, validated for solvability, and pruned of underspecified items or brittle hacks. Tasks were stratified post hoc into Easy/Medium/Hard tiers (30%/40%/30%) based on aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters eliminated incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive entries to curate an initial task pool.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist drafted by Hunyuan-Turbos and refined by human experts. A 10% manually curated seed was used to anchor calibration and serve as few-shot references. For validation, a double-blind human study on 280 queries and 6 models was conducted, where annotators independently scored outputs and the median rating was used as the ground truth.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement on the 10% calibration seed achieved Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8. In the human validation study, pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC) was measured between human ratings (the median of annotator scores) and MLLM-as-Judge scores, reaching up to 90.95% agreement.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Engineers with extensive front-end development experience.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None; queries were screened via a quality filtering stage ensuring they avoid requesting or involving sensitive personal information such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Minor discrepancies observed in fine-grained scoring reflect potential cognitive biases in how different MLLMs interpret long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Discrete sampling via three staged screenshots at fixed intervals may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions (such as multi-step user workflows or nuanced game physics). Additionally, it focuses on single-turn generation rather than agentic, iterative multi-turn development and debugging.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating the visual fidelity, interactive integrity, and code quality of Large Language Models on interactive visual code generation tasks.
